candidates.title: PRT stored player reopen adopts the unsynced backup's cached hash tree and discards the guaranteed epoch machine (wrong hashes after a power loss during commit)
candidates.component: PRT stored player (doc/recipes/prt.lua), run by crisium as the honest validator
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'); stands in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua: get_stored_root_hash (~l.2850), revert_interrupted_input (~l.2864-2881), stored_machine_pair_methods:commit (~l.1137-1149), new_stored_machine (~l.1007, loads without clear_hash_tree), reopen_epoch_directory (~l.3076, l.3102)
candidates.description: stored_machine_pair_methods:commit destroys the epoch machine, syncs <epoch>/machine (now a directory O2 guarantees, holding the boundary that state.json already records), removes machine.revert, clone_stored(machine -> machine.revert) and only then sync_stored(machine.revert). A power loss between the clone and the end of its sync leaves machine.revert in an unspecified state; get_stored_root_hash's own comment says so: 'A clone is durable only after its sync, so after a power loss its cached hash tree may not match its contents'. On reopen, revert_interrupted_input calls get_stored_root_hash(machine.revert), which loads it with clear_hash_tree=true (rebuilt only in memory, no sharing) and compares the content hash with state.json's root_hash. When the contents match it takes branch 1: it REMOVES <epoch>/machine (the guaranteed, synced copy that also holds root_hash) and clone_stored(machine.revert -> machine), which copies the backup's on-disk dht/dpt/sht/phtc files unchanged. reopen_epoch_directory then calls new_stored_machine(root_hash, machine), which loads with SHARING_ALL and WITHOUT clear_hash_tree, so the stale cached hash-tree data the content check deliberately bypassed becomes the epoch machine's hash tree. The root assert passes whenever the stale data is in a subtree the dirty-page tree marks clean (the cached root is still right), but the tree is internally inconsistent: proofs of that page are wrong, and the next change to a sibling page combines the stale leaf hash into a wrong root hash, i.e. a wrong computation-hash leaf and wrong claims for the rest of the epoch. The next commit then clones the corrupted tree into the new backup, so it never self-heals. The fix is to rebuild on adoption (load the clone with clear_hash_tree, or rebuild then store), to prefer the guaranteed machine directory when it holds root_hash, or to create the backup as <dir>.revert.tmp + sync + rename_stored so machine.revert is only ever a synced directory.
candidates.trigger: No adversary: the unlucky honest operator's host loses power while the stored player commits an input boundary (after clone_stored(machine, machine.revert) and before sync_stored(machine.revert) completes), with the backup's data files durable but some cached hash-tree blocks (dht/dpt/sht) not. The operator restarts crisium exactly as documented (reopen from the epoch directory).
candidates.reachability: Each accepted input boundary performs this commit, so the window is hit on every input. O2 states that a directory being written when its process stopped is in an unspecified state: 'A stop at any other point ... can leave registers, memory and the hash tree in a combination that no execution reaches', and the player's own comment acknowledges that the cached hash tree may not match its contents. Data blocks durable while hash-tree blocks are not is an ordinary writeback order on a copying (non-reflink) filesystem. I could not cut power; I reproduced the post-crash on-disk state by flipping one leaf hash in machine.revert's RAM .dht after a normal commit, which matches 'cached hash tree may not match its contents' exactly.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The exclusion 'Defects that need the honest operator to reload a stored directory that O2 does not guarantee' covers an operator that reloads such a directory, but here the shipped reference operator itself chooses to resume from the non-guaranteed backup and discard the guaranteed one. Section 5: 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too. The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them.' O2: 'The operator discards those directories and resumes from a guaranteed one'. The trigger is a host fault (power loss), and section 4 says the emulator 'must never turn one into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state'. So it is not excluded. 2. Role: the PRT player in doc/recipes is Support (AUDIT.md table); it is an 'implementation of an operator' that stands in for the honest operator. 3. High/Medium cases: section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. In the honest-operator role this is Critical (step 4 reasoning): a wrong hash and a lost guaranteed copy on the honest operator's path. So it is Medium. 4. (For the stand-in role) R1: 'Cached hash-tree data ... On the honest operator's path, it was either written by the operator's own process into a directory that O2 guarantees, or rebuilt from the contents on adoption (O1)'; here it is neither. R9: 'The content hash must equal the root of the actual contents'. Section 1 completeness failure: 'The honest operator computes a wrong hash'. R4: 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim.' 5. n/a.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support component; Critical in the honest-operator role it stands in for)
candidates.threat_to_goal: A validator built on this recipe, after one power loss at the wrong moment, silently commits to wrong computation hashes for the remaining inputs of the epoch (completeness failure: its honest claim is eliminated and a dishonest claim can win), and it has deleted the only guaranteed copy that would let it recover. The emulator itself behaves as documented; the reference operator breaks O1/O2 and R1.
candidates.evidence: Scratch /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERFAULT/player1.lua, player2.lua, probe.lua. (a) prt.new_stored_player on a copy of bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template/machine creates epoch/ (state.json root 0x428a6b..., machine and machine.revert both verify). (b) I flipped one bit of the leaf hash of page 0x82000000 in epoch/machine.revert/0000000080000000-4000000.dht (offset 786432); probe of epoch/machine before reopen: cached root 0x428a6b..., verify_hash_tree true. (c) Reopening with prt.new_stored_player gives epoch machine root 0x428a6b... (assert passes) but verify_hash_tree=false ('page 0x82000000 (in RAM) is not marked dirty but is dirty'). epoch/machine is now the clone of the corrupted backup. (d) After a write to the neighbouring page 0x82001000 (standing in for a guest store), the cached root is 0x2cc3f6... while the content root (store + clear_hash_tree) is 0x29cceb..., so later hashes are wrong.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: create a stored player epoch directory from the baremetal template, close it, flip one leaf in machine.revert's RAM .dht for a page the guest never touches (simulating the documented post-power-loss state of an unsynced clone), reopen with prt.new_stored_player, then assert (1) p.epoch_pair.machine:verify_hash_tree() is true, and (2) after advancing the machine or writing a neighbouring page, get_root_hash() equals the clear_hash_tree rebuild of the same contents. Optionally also assert that epoch/machine, which was synced and held root_hash, was not replaced by the unsynced backup. Exit 1 on audit/prt2, 0 once reopen rebuilds or avoids the unsynced backup.

candidates.title: CLI --revert-mode=stored crash-recovery rule discards the only good copies when a kill or power loss interrupts the removal of <dir>.revert
candidates.component: cartesi-machine CLI stored revert mode (src/cartesi-machine.lua) and its manual and --help recovery rule; same pattern in doc/recipes/run-rolling-calculator-from-storage.lua
candidates.role: Support (the cartesi-machine CLI and the Lua recipes; AUDIT.md table). Stands in for the honest operator's 'storing and reloading' and 'restarting after a stop' path
candidates.location: src/cartesi-machine.lua revert_stored.__index:commit (~l.3893-3918: remove_stored(old .revert) before rename of .revert.tmp), revert_stored.__index:remove_backup (~l.3934) and the exit path (~l.4925-4932); help text l.158-175; doc/README.md 'Rolling Cartesi Machines directly from storage' (~l.2522-2540) and the Lua 'Rolling Cartesi Machines directly from storage' section (~l.5537-5576); src/machine.cpp machine::remove_stored (unlinks the files one by one, config last, then rmdir)
candidates.description: At every commit the CLI destroys the machine, syncs <dir>, clones it to <dir>.revert.tmp, syncs the clone, then calls remove_stored(<dir>.revert) and only afterwards renames .revert.tmp to .revert. remove_stored is not atomic: it unlinks each data/dht/dpt/hash-tree file, then config.json, then rmdirs. A kill or power loss partway leaves a <dir>.revert directory that still exists but is missing files. The manual and --help tell the operator: 'If machine.revert exists, it holds that state, so discard machine and machine.revert.tmp and clone machine.revert back to machine' (--help: 'after a crash or kill, resume from <directory>.revert if it exists ... discard <directory>.revert.tmp in every case'). Following that rule exactly discards <dir> (synced and holding the newly committed state) and <dir>.revert.tmp (a synced, complete clone of it), and then fails to clone the broken .revert. All copies of the committed state are lost and the run has to start over from the template. The clean-exit path has the same gap: it syncs <dir> and then remove_stored(<dir>.revert), so an interruption there makes the rule discard the synced final machine. The Lua recipe documented for the same scheme (commit removes backup_directory before rename_stored) has the same window. A fix is to rename the old backup to an unambiguous name (such as <dir>.revert.old, through the atomic rename_stored) before removing it, and to state the rule by complete names, or to make remove_stored first rename the directory atomically.
candidates.trigger: No adversary: the honest operator's process is killed, or the host loses power, during the removal of the old <dir>.revert at any accepted input (each commit) or at clean exit. The operator then follows the manual's recovery rule exactly.
candidates.reachability: Every accepted input performs the remove-then-rename. Reproduced with a real SIGKILL injected by strace at the 6th unlink of machine.revert during the second commit.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is a kill or host fault followed by the documented recovery rule, not a reload by the operator of a directory O2 does not guarantee. The rule itself tells the operator to discard the guaranteed directories and to resume from one that was being removed. Section 5: 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too. The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them, and the emulator must make them possible to follow.' Not excluded. 2. Role: the CLI is Support (AUDIT.md table: 'the cartesi-machine CLI ... Support'), standing in for the honest operator's storing, reloading and restarting. 3. High/Medium cases: section 8: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' The manual says machine.revert 'always holds a synced copy of the last committed state' and that 'If machine.revert exists, it holds that state'. Section 3: support defects are 'Medium when [they] would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. For the honest operator, losing every guaranteed copy breaks R4 ('After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim') and O2 ('resumes from a guaranteed one'), which is Critical if replay from the template cannot meet the clocks, or the Medium case 'A persistence operation that fails loudly, without a wrong hash ... while cleaning up after a stop' if it can. 4. (Stand-in role) R4 restart clause and O2 as quoted. 5. If triage reads it as a pure loud failure with replay always possible, it is Low (a defect in a tool) or Medium (persistence failing loudly while cleaning up after a stop).
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support; manual contradiction on a recovery rule). Low if replay from the template is considered always affordable
candidates.threat_to_goal: An operator following the documented recovery for the stored mode loses the committed state and every guaranteed copy of it after a single kill at the wrong moment, and must replay the epoch from the template, which may not fit the dispute clocks. No wrong hash is produced (the broken directory fails to clone loudly), but the documented 'guaranteed copy' invariant is false.
candidates.evidence: Scratch dir .../blind10/PERFAULT (recover.lua, trace2.txt). Command: strace -f -e trace=unlink -e inject=unlink:signal=KILL:when=84 lua5.4 src/cartesi-machine.lua --revert-mode=stored --load=machine,clone:<baremetal-template>/machine,sharing:all --cmio-advance-state=input:input-%i.bin,input_file_index_begin:0,input_file_index_end:3,output_proof:,output:out-%o-%i.bin,report:rep-%o-%i.bin --final-hash. It was killed at unlink('machine.revert/0000000000010000-1000.dpt'). Left on disk: machine, machine.revert (22 of 27 files), machine.revert.tmp (27 files). Following the rule: clone_stored('machine.revert', ...) fails ('open() failed: No such file or directory'), and loading machine.revert fails too, while machine.revert.tmp, which the rule says to discard, loads fine (mcycle 3526372, the committed boundary).
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh: run the stored-mode command above under strace with inject=unlink:signal=KILL at an unlink inside the old .revert removal, then apply the manual's rule mechanically (if <dir>.revert exists: clone it back to <dir>) and assert that the clone succeeds and yields the root hash of the last committed boundary, which machine.revert.tmp holds. Exit 1 on audit/prt2. Alternatively, assert the invariant that the name <dir>.revert never refers to an incomplete directory at any SIGKILL point in a commit.

not_covered: fsync error semantics (fsyncgate): whether a retried sync_stored after an EIO or ENOSPC from fsync can report success for data the kernel dropped. Not testable deterministically here, and no retry site was found on the player or CLI paths.
Real power-loss and writeback-ordering experiments (no dm-flakey/dm-log-writes available); candidate 1 simulates the post-crash state instead.

Allocation failures (std::bad_alloc) inside hash_tree::update or update_dirty_pages mid-update, and whether a machine that keeps running afterwards stays consistent (R9 'interrupted or failed updates'); only skimmed.
File-descriptor exhaustion (EMFILE) during load, clone or store with many flash drives, and the JSON-RPC server (remote machine, fork, rebind) under timeouts or killed servers: not examined.

The CLI resumable epoch files (begin_epoch:false, state_hash, outputs_frontier, computation-hash frontier): the manual already documents that they need manual repair after a crash; not audited further.

prt-bridge.lua decision logic after restarts (only the journal in prt-transactions.lua and crisium's startup and removal logic were read); prt-epoch.lua listener re-delivery after restart only skimmed.
Machine cache entries, the agreed pair, and checkpoint creation across power loss in prt.lua: read, no defect found (removal after commit, durable rename of checkpoints).
--store without sync in the CLI (the manual makes no durability claim for it), and the macOS F_FULLFSYNC path.
Disk-full during machine::store or clone_stored (scope_remove cleanup paths) was read, not exercised.
